correctness.rationale: For \(f(x)=Lx^2/2\), the source Bregman-type curvature quantity is exactly \(L(x_k-x_{k-1})^2/2\), so the branch condition is precisely \(\lambda_{k-1}>2\eta_0/L\) and the reset value is exactly \(2\eta_1/L\). Consecutive resets require disjoint expansion-factor blocks whose products exceed \(\eta_0/\eta_1\), giving the reset-count bound. After the last reset the positive expansion factors produce a monotone bounded stepsize sequence with limit in \((2\eta_1/L,2\eta_0/L]\). An exponential dyadic tail realizes every such limit. The iterate recurrence \(x_{k+1}=(1-L\lambda_k)x_k\) then gives the exact asymptotic ratio.

value.rationale: The adaptive stepsize is the main algorithmic novelty of the source. On the canonical strongly convex mode, the finding completely characterizes that mechanism: when resets occur, how many can occur, where the terminal stepsize can land, and the exact resulting asymptotic rate. It also explains why the paper's near-equal parameter pair \(0.5,0.49\) is exceptionally aggressive after a reset while showing that the no-reset branch can still be arbitrarily slow. This is a natural exact invariant of the proposed controller rather than an arbitrary special-case calculation.
